LESSON: INTERACTIVE SPEAKING TURN TAKING NONVERBAL COMMUNICATION INTONATION QUESTIONING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.9: Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: how to move around, (Comment va-t-on en ville?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement
2. use vocabulary and expressions appropriately to probe and engage in oral interactions
3. use non-verbal communication cues to enhance communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning

Teach
• Focus skill: respond to questions and prompts to show comprehension and engagement.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how to move around, (Comment va-t-on en ville?
2. How else can you express yourself without talking?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
